_comment: MCP servers for the Stage 3 executor. The Chrome extension used for local
browser work does not exist on a build node, so headless Playwright is the
driver here.
--browser chrome is deliberate. Without it Playwright MCP launches its own
bundled chromium, which is a second browser to install and keep matched on a
node that already has Google Chrome for the Dusk suite (Dusk requires a real
Chrome plus a version-matched chromedriver). One browser, three consumers:
this server and php artisan dusk. On a node with no
system Chrome, drop the flag and run `playwright install chromium` instead.
--ignore-https-errors is not optional here. The instance is served over TLS by
ci/qa/tls-proxy.php with a self-signed certificate, because AppServiceProvider
calls URL::forceScheme('https') unconditionally. Without the flag EVERY
navigation dies on net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID — measured against a live
instance on 2026-08-21 — and the agent, unable to open a single page, reports
that the browser was unavailable and falls back to driving the specs through
Bash. The rest of the harness already agreed on this: the probes pass
PROBE_INSECURE=1, DuskTestCase passes --ignore-certificate-errors and
--allow-insecure-localhost. This config was the one piece that did not.
The QA Touch MCP server is deliberately NOT used: Stage 3 calls the API
through ci/qa/qatouch-client.sh so both stages share one client and one set
of documented workarounds. See ci/qa/qatouch-facts.md.
